g.text: Rate Limiter: the algorithm behind the interface, and where atomicity has to live
Left: two swappable algorithms over one swappable store. Right: why the store must be atomic, not the caller.
The race: two requests, one token
Naive read-then-write: both see 1, both decide 'allowed', both write 0.
Budget of 1 just let 2 requests through.
Fix: Redis INCR (atomic) or a Lua script -- read+refill+write
as one step the store guarantees isn't interleaved.
